analysis: The PR modifies only docs/architecture/inference.md; no source code, config or deployment behavior changes. The supplied units (head text lines 1-797) are documentation of the Nemotron Super managed slot, load fit, prefix bank, image/video admission, and GLM5Next boundaries. The visible patch hunks (CBv2 scheduler geometry table: wider prefill chunk 2048/4096 for GPT-OSS, dense Qwen3.5/3.8, Gemma 4; bidirectionalMediaPrefillChunkCeiling) fall outside the numbered excerpts in these units (head ranges 1087-1090, 1100-1146, 2028-2041), so I could not verify them line by line. I examined the documented security-relevant claims against the threat model: prefix-cache text reuse is described as partitioned by authenticated cache scope and off without one (consistent with T-041 account-scoped cacheSalt; image requests without scope stay cold and never publish). The slot emits no cache receipts or cached-token usage, so no new at-rest SSD artifact is described for Super (the bank is resident RAM, carved from the paged grant), which is a distinct surface from the T-041 SSD tier; the T-041 text says production never constructs a resident-RAM prefix cache, so the Super resident hybrid checkpoint bank (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1, managed slot default-on when grant allows) is a documented in-process cross-request cache whose TTFT oracle is scoped by tenant, but the threat model's statement of 'no production RAM tier' may now be stale. This is a documentation-vs-model drift for the next pass to reconcile, not a demonstrable regression from this PR diff alone (the bank behavior may predate it). Media admission (8 MiB body cap, ingress/media charges before decode, 429/503/400 mappings, decode time allowance) are availability controls consistent with T-029/T-050 style concerns; no weakening is evident. No finding qualifies; I flag deeper review only for the unseen patch lines and the Super resident prefix bank versus T-041 wording.
